findings.claim: Change #2 allows curl/wget whenever the body goes to a file. It drops v1's silent-flag and verbose-flag conditions, so the stderr progress-meter flood that #166's fix blocked comes back. Golden case line 58 tests only the -s variant.
findings.evidence: v1 hooks/core/routing.mjs:755-762 'Must be silent ... to prevent progress bar stderr flood'; tests/hooks/core-routing.test.ts:178 'blocks curl -o file WITHOUT silent flag' and :186 'blocks curl -o file with --verbose'. These v1 tests must pass (owner decision).
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 2731ca25 2026-03-22 'feat: allow curl/wget with silent file-output, block stdout floods (#166)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'Example blocked: curl -o file url (no -s, progress bar floods stderr)'. REGRESSION_RISK: high, re-breaks #166's guard. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: a pipeline counts as safe only when both stdout and stderr are bounded (-s/-q present or 2>file/2>/dev/null, and no -v/--verbose/--trace/-D -).
findings.fix: Define 'body reaches tool output' over stdout AND stderr. Add golden cases: 'curl -L -o f url' gives deny, 'curl -s --verbose -o f url' gives deny.

findings.claim: The decision looks only at each simple command's argv0. Wrapper commands (sudo, time, env, nice, timeout, xargs, command) and command substitution put curl outside argv0. v1's regex catches these, so an argv0-only parser lets them through.
findings.evidence: node test of v1 regex /(^|\s|&&|\||\;)(curl|wget)\s/i: 'sudo curl -s https://x' true, 'time curl -s https://x' true, 'echo u | xargs curl -s' true, 'x=$(curl -s https://x)' false. The ADR names no wrapper list, no rule for $(...) and no rule for bash -c / sh -c strings.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 3383299c 2026-03-05 'Fix false-positive HTTP regex matching inside quoted arguments' (line 733). The original block was fbf402fd 2026-02-25 'unified PreToolUse hook — block Bash data-fetching'. REGRESSION_RISK: fail-open on common wrappers. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep v1 detection coverage as a minimum.
findings.fix: Specify a fixed list of wrapper commands whose first operand becomes the effective argv0. Recurse into $(...), backticks and the string argument of bash/sh/zsh -c. Add GP3 rows for sudo, xargs, $(curl ...) and bash -c 'curl ...'.

findings.claim: Inline HTTP (fetch(, requests.get(, http.get() lives inside a quoted -e/-c argument, not in argv0 or flags. The ADR does not say how the regex-free parser finds it. v1 tests require these to be blocked.
findings.evidence: v1 routing.mjs:793-797 (regex over the heredoc-stripped command); tests/hooks/core-routing.test.ts:211 'node -e "fetch(...)"', :223 'python -c "...requests.get(...)"'; omp-plugin.test.ts:127,136; integration.test.ts:179.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 49694ea0 2026-03-05 'heredoc-aware routing' (noHeredoc); first added in fbf402fd 2026-02-25. ORIGINAL_INTENT (code comment): 'strip only heredocs (not quotes) so that code passed via -e/-c flags is still visible'. REGRESSION_RISK: inline HTTP gets through. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: inspect the -e/-c/--eval operand of node, python, ruby, perl and deno with a token scan, not a regex.
findings.fix: Add a rule: for interpreter argv0 with an eval flag, run a literal token scan on the eval operand. List it in GP3, and include the heredoc-to-interpreter case (python <<EOF ... requests.get).

findings.claim: ParseError means allow. So any command that also has [[, ((, case or a function is fully allowed, for example '[[ -f x ]] && curl -s https://x.io/a.json'. v1 denies this. This fails open on a common bash idiom.
findings.evidence: ADR-0008:51 'Result: allow and journal the code'. v1 routing.mjs:733 matches curl anywhere in the stripped string, so v1 denies.
findings.archaeology: v1 detection is from fbf402fd/3383299c (see above). REGRESSION_RISK: easy bypass. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no fallback chain (owner), so the one path must not be blind allow.
findings.fix: Treat unsupported constructs as opaque nodes and still run the decision on the simple commands that parse, or support [[ ]] and (( )) as test nodes. Add a GP3 row for '[[ … ]] && curl -s url' that expects deny.

findings.claim: The 'bounded sink' list has no numeric bound and an undefined rule. 'head -c N' with any N, and 'jq with a scalar', cannot be decided without a cap and a jq program analysis.
findings.evidence: ADR-0008:25 '(head -c N, wc, grep -c, jq with a scalar …)'. The trailing '…' leaves the list open. No N limit is tied to the output budget.
findings.fix: Make the sink list closed and exact. Require N ≤ the output budget (the same B as ADR-0016). Drop 'jq with a scalar', or define it as a closed set of jq filters (length, .field|type …).

findings.claim: The ratio sort has no tie-break. Equal ratios are common: the same weight, age and size, or age 0 in one turn. Without a total order, the 'same rows → same bytes' claim depends on the sort's stability and the input order.
findings.evidence: ADR-0009:73-74 'Take items in ratio order' with no secondary key. :89 claims '10 runs out of 10 identical'. That is one machine and one engine, not a proof.
findings.fix: State a total order: ratio desc, then seq desc (or asc). Compare by integer cross-multiplication (s1*b2 vs s2*b1) so float rounding cannot change the order.

findings.claim: 'Score (integers only)' contradicts the formula. 0.75·2^(−age/4), 0.7^k and score/bytes are not integers, and no scale factor is given.
findings.fix: Give fixed-point scales (e.g. decay ×1000 in the table, 0.7^k as an integer table ×1000) and the exact integer ratio comparison.

findings.claim: There are 5 sections × 85 = 425 candidates, but §4 says at most 340. Also, the ADR does not say which 85 rows a section keeps when it has more (newest? highest score?), and that choice changes the output for the 10,000-row golden case.
findings.evidence: ADR-0009:58 'Each section gives at most 85 candidates', :50-56 five sections, :77 'At most 340 candidates'.
findings.fix: Say 'pinned prompt + 4×85 = 341', or fix the number. State the per-section cap order (e.g. top 85 by score, ties broken by seq desc).

findings.claim: Open-error keys are defined for cmd and toolerr, but the ADR does not say how a failed edit (kind edit, ok=0) is keyed or resolved, or whether it is an open error at all. Its weight is not in the table either.
findings.evidence: ADR-0009:36 'edit: Write/Edit file path, ok/fail'. :38-39 give keys only for cmd/toolerr. :63 weights have no entry for a failed edit.
findings.fix: State: failed edit key = tool + path, resolved by a later ok edit of the same path, weight 900.

findings.claim: Chunk selection has no budget number. v1 chunks can be up to 4,096 B. If the budget is ADR-0009's 2,048 B, a single top chunk never fits, and the subagent gets only the 'more:' line. The ADR also does not say what happens when there is no intent ('description' is optional), because then every BM25 score is 0 and the selection order is not defined.
findings.evidence: ADR-0016:27,30 'up to the budget' with no value. v1 src/store.ts:153 'const MAX_CHUNK_BYTES = 4096' (609a3a5a 2026-03-03). ADR-0016:27 intent = 'the call's description field'.
findings.fix: Fix the budget B in bytes and require MAX_CHUNK_BYTES ≤ B (or chunk to ≤ B/2 for subagent output). Define no-intent selection (e.g. chunks in seq order from the start and the end). Define the output order (seq order) and the tie-break.

findings.claim: The ADR does not say which subagent Bash calls are rewritten. 'The same output budget applies in every context' and LV9 ('a 5 MB output command') imply every large command. But ADR-0008 dropped size-prediction deny, and line 32 limits the scope to the curl/wget/build cases. If only the deny scope is rewritten, 'cat big.log' still floods the subagent, and the MUST in ADR-0016 fails.
findings.evidence: ADR-0016:14, :32, :50 (LV9); ADR-0008:18 'The r2 deny of any Bash call whose predicted output is too large is dropped'.
findings.fix: State one rule. Either case B wraps every Bash call of a subagent without ctx tools (run.mjs passes small output through whole), or name the exact set. Make the GP3 rows match.

covered: ADR-0008 parser, per-pipeline sink rule, parse errors, golden cases vs v1 routing.mjs and tests
